key_concepts: The circulatory system transports oxygen and nutrients to body cells.
Blood acts as the cargo that carries oxygen and nutrients.
Blood vessels are the pathways that carry blood throughout the body.
Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
Veins carry blood back toward the heart.
The heart is a fist-sized muscular organ located slightly left of the chest center.
The heart pumps blood continuously and cannot be controlled voluntarily.
The heart has receiving chambers called atria and pumping chambers called ventricles.
Valves in the heart keep blood flowing in one direction.

Physical activity increases heart rate, which can be felt as pulse at the wrist.
